title: Spending actions and a smaller state for value iteration
question: With three spending actions (economy, army, research) and a smaller state (cities, income, units, techs; with and without the turn), does value iteration give a policy that beats the bot and comes closer to research every turn than experiment 21's policy?
change: Actions: spend3 (economy = build, army = train and attack, research; each x2 for one turn; no 'bot' action, states without a policy entry play the bot unchanged). State: (cities, income, units, techs) and (turn, cities, income, units, techs) on the same data; without the turn, value iteration sweeps until the values settle (at most 30 sweeps).
method: 300k games with a random spend3 action per turn; value iteration for both state versions and min-count 1, 5, 20, 50; min-count chosen per version on 2,000 validation seeds; both chosen policies on the 10,000 evaluation seeds
setups: Perfection, 16×16 continents, 4 players, Crazy, seat 0 Xin-Xi (human seat), learner base greedy-full-probe-perf; opponents greedy-full-probe-perf, greedy-full-combo-perf, greedy-full-probe-perf (anchor), seats shuffled per seed (rl-gate defaults)
